newsitem.title: CHILE: CHILE DEPUTIES CALL FOR PROBE INTO CODELCO DEAL.
newsitem.headline: CHILE DEPUTIES CALL FOR PROBE INTO CODELCO DEAL.

text.p: Chilean rightist National Renovation Party deputies said they will ask Congress to investigate an accord to resolve a dispute over futures trades between state copper company Codelco and Minera El Bronce.
El Bronce agreed last month to pay Codelco $6.4 million to settle a spat over loss-making futures trades carried out by former Codelco futures operator Juan Pablo Davila.
Under the pact, Codelco agreed not to bring a civil case in the Chilean courts against El Bronce.

A former Codelco director, Fernando Molina, told a Congress commission Tuesday that that the corporation had made a mistake and the losses caused by Davila's deals with El Bronce were higher than the $6.4 million estimate.
The pact with El Bronce has been criticized by congressmen and local media as being too generous to the private mining firm.
Minera El Bronce is owned by the family of former Codelco CEO Alejandro Noemi who resigned in disgrace after the losses were revealed in early 1994.
Codelco lost $175 million in 1993 as a result of failed futures deals carried out by Davila, the then top futures trader at the corporation.
